CalCOFI's hydrographic time series began in 1949 with weather, temperature, salinity, oxygen, and phosphate measurements; nutrient analysis expanded to include silicate, nitrate, and nitrite in 1961, chlorophyll was added in 1973, and carbon-14 primary productivity incubations were added in 1984. The dataset covers primarily the CalCOFI station grid off Southern and Central California, with broader coverage extending farther north, south, and offshore during early cruises, and spans 1949 to 2020. This dataset supports long-term study of phytoplankton biomass and productivity trends in the California Current, for researchers studying multi-decade changes in primary production

holdings.description_md: Baleen Whale Density Prediction from Environmental DNA (eDNA) contains processed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) abundance tables for three eDNA markers, 16S rRNA, 18S rRNA V4, and 18S rRNA V9, developed by Erin Satterthwaite, Trevor Ruiz, Nastassia Patin, and colleagues to test whether microbial and small zooplankton communities can predict the density of baleen whales in the southern California Current Ecosystem. The dataset covers CalCOFI cruises in the southern California Current Ecosystem and spans 2014 to 2020, combining eDNA data from the NOAA CalCOFI Genomics Program (NCOG) with line-transect distance-sampling density estimates for blue, fin, and humpback whales derived from CalCOFI whale sighting surveys. The data are analyzed using stability selection adapted to sparse partial least squares (sPLS) regression, a statistical method for identifying reliable microbial and zooplankton predictors of whale density within large sequencing datasets. Processed data includes ASV tables with taxonomic annotations, sample metadata, density estimates, and cross-validation partitions. This dataset supports research on eDNA-based indicators of marine mammal distribution and is intended for researchers studying whale ecology and biomonitoring methods in the California Current.

holdings.description_md: CalCOFI Size-Fractionated Chlorophyll a (>8µm / <8µm) contains depth-integrated chlorophyll a biomass split by cell size (larger and smaller than 8 μm), along with zooplankton displacement volume and nitracline depth, generated by Michael Mullin, Director of the Marine Life Research Group (UC San Diego), from samples collected aboard California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) cruises off the coast of California. The dataset covers twelve quarterly CalCOFI cruises and spans January 1994 to October 1996. At roughly half the stations sampled on each cruise, water was collected at multiple depths using closing bottles on a CTD rosette; chlorophyll from each bottle was retained on a GF/F glass-fiber filter and measured fluorometrically, while an additional combined sample from the shallowest ten bottles (surface to about 100 m) was filtered through an 8 μm membrane filter to isolate the larger size fraction. Total and ≥8 μm chlorophyll were each integrated to 100 m depth, and chlorophyll <8 μm was calculated as the difference between the two. This dataset supports research relating phytoplankton size structure to nitracline depth and zooplankton grazing pressure, for researchers studying controls on phytoplankton community size composition in the California Current.

holdings.description_md: CalCOFI Phytoplankton Community Taxon-Specific Pigments contains concentrations of chlorophyll and other pigments used to estimate phytoplankton biomass and taxonomic composition, collected during California Current Ecosystem Long-Term Ecological Research (CCE-LTER) Process cruises, periodic research cruises distinct from the routine quarterly California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) survey. Samples are collected from rosette bottles at three to eight depths in the photic zone at stations within the California Current Ecosystem region, spanning 2006 to 2017. Particulate matter is filtered and frozen at sea, then extracted onshore for High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) analysis, which measures chlorophyll and carotenoid pigment concentrations. Chlorophyll a concentration serves as a proxy for total phytoplankton biomass, while other taxon-specific pigments are used to determine the contribution of different phytoplankton taxa to that biomass.
